conflicts: Fravor's sworn statement that 'tapes were never taken' is in direct tension with the accounts attributed to USS Princeton crewmen Kevin Day and Gary Voorhis that recording media were removed by unidentified personnel who arrived by helicopter. Both can be true if the collection was aimed at Princeton's Aegis and CEC data and at Nimitz's ATFLIR tape library rather than at VFA-41 aircrew, whom Fravor confirms were never even debriefed.

label: David Fravor
narrative: Fravor is the aviator whose single intercept broke the observational record open. In November 2004 he was Commanding Officer of Strike Fighter Squadron Forty-One, the Black Aces, attached to Carrier Air Wing Eleven aboard USS Nimitz. In his sworn written statement to the House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border and Foreign Affairs on 26 July 2023 he described being vectored off a training intercept to investigate a contact the cruiser USS Princeton had been tracking, and finding 'a small white Tic Tac shaped object with the longitudinal axis pointing N/S and moving very abruptly over the white water,' with 'no Rotors, No Rotor wash, or any visible flight control surfaces.' He testified the Princeton had been watching objects descend from above 80,000 feet to 20,000 feet 'for the previous 2 weeks.' The single most load-bearing line in his statement is a negative one: 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.' That sentence is not a denial of the coverup - it is evidence of the specific shape of it. The Navy's own range fouler report on the incident, released via FOIA on 13 January 2023, records that 'Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.' The event stayed dormant until Jay Stratton contacted Fravor in 2009 to investigate it for a DoD program, and until the New York Times published the FLIR1 video in December 2017. Fravor told 60 Minutes on 16 May 2021 the object 'was aware we were there' and that 'it just disappears. Like, gone.'
